fixed.how: daemon/pull-requests.ts: goneUnder (was buildsOnGone) names the tasks a pressed chain builds on whose pull request is not listed open and not merged on its record. After the chain's own branch check, settleClosedAtPress reads each of them once with getPullRequest, also when that check refuses (the two early returns now break out first). One closed without a merge goes to the new closedAtPress port. session/dependent-branches.ts: closedAtPress runs closedOnHost with rebuild: false. It sets the record to '#1 was closed without merging.' (or merged through another), closes its merge cards and settles the row, as the watcher's report would. What built on it is not rebuilt there: the press's check already rebuilt the chain, and the next poll, which reads the close again, rebuilds the rest. So the press writes to GitHub only for what the person pressed. An open dependency (task redone or cancelled) or one merged on GitHub is left to that poll, whose report tells the merge's listeners once. A failed read is logged and left to the poll. compose.ts wires the port and emits a project event. The fake daemon's pullRequestPressFinds takes closedDependency and settles that task's record the same way.

not_done.problem: L4-github-124 (b) and (c): the cancelled block's plural for one pull request; a pull request rebuilt without its dependency is still listed under 'Reviewed by the critic'.
not_done.why: The spec's cut line allows these two. This fixup built only part (a), which the cut line does not allow to be left out.

not_done.problem: A dependency that was merged on GitHub (not closed) shortly before the press still reads 'waiting for you to merge' until the watcher's next poll.
not_done.why: This was done on purpose. Settling a merge at the press would either start the merge's listeners there (copy refresh, card closing, and rebuilds of other dependents, which are GitHub writes the person did not press) or leave them unheard, because the poll skips a record already marked merged. The item and its acceptance name the closed dependency, and that case is fixed. ADR 0111's 2026-11-23 amendment, point 5, says so.

new_problems: A paused run that no run has continued yet counts as one try in Costs. While the task waits on its Continue card, By task reads '0 / 1 (0%)' (views.ts taskRunFacts adds a run to `continued` only once a later run exists). ADR 0112 point 5 says a paused run is no failed try. A paused run should probably count no try until it is continued or cancelled. The new test does not pin either behaviour (it asserts only runs 1, accepted 0 before Continue).

The press's settle reads each gone dependency once with getPullRequest. That is one more read-only GET per closed dependency per press, and only when the chain builds on a pull request that is no longer listed open.
